ev.q: Among 214.4 million eligible persons aged ≥5 years, 106.3 million (49.6%) received a booster dose
Among 58.8 million persons aged ≥50 years who were eligible to receive a second booster dose, 20.0 million (34.0%) received a second booster
Among this population, 106.3 million (49.6%) received a booster dose
Second booster dose coverage increased with age, ranging from 26.1% among persons aged 50–64 years
Among 214 million eligible persons aged ≥5 years, approximately one half received a booster dose
Booster coverage was lower among males (47.3%) than among females (51.9%)
When stratified by age group, the lowest booster dose coverage among persons aged 5–39 years was among Black persons
Data on COVID-19 vaccine administration in the United States are reported to CDC by jurisdictions, pharmacies, and federal entities.

methods_quotes.q: Tests for statistical significance were not conducted because these data are reflective of the U.S. population aged ≥5 years
Booster dose vaccination coverage was calculated among persons who completed a primary series
A booster dose was defined as a homologous or heterologous dose of COVID-19 vaccine administered ≥4 weeks
A 4-day grace period was subtracted from all interval calculations to allow for doses received ≤4 days earlier than recommended.
